summary: Windows Update rollback leaves device in 'Pending Cleanup' loop after SSD replacement
description: Issue summary: Several Dell Latitude devices are failing to complete provisioning after a depot SSD replacement. Instead of completing the SCCM task sequence / OOBE, machines boot to a Windows sign-in screen with a notification 'Pending Cleanup' and several pending updates that restart the rollback flow. This prevents imaging or autopilot re-enrollment and requires manual intervention.
impact: Affected ~8 devices this week from the repair pool. Blocks re-provisioning of repaired hardware; escalates time-to-fulfill RMA returns and increases hardware MTTR. No customer-facing outage but measurable backlog for depot team.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replace SSD in Dell Latitude (depot repair workflow).
2) Boot device to SCCM PXE task sequence and apply corporate image (TS applies drivers, SCCM Windows Update step).

3) Task sequence completes and device restarts into OOBE. Expected: autopilot enrollment or join. Actual: Windows boots to sign-in with 'Pending Cleanup' toast and Windows Update shows 'Rollback in progress' or 'Pending Cleanup'.
4) Attempts to re-run task sequence from USB/PXE fail due to pending reboot/update state; smsts.log shows Exit code 3010 or scheduled restart stuck.
logs: smsts.log excerpt 2026-03-09T14:12:45Z: TS Progress: Steps complete. Returning exit code 3010 (reboot required).
WindowsUpdate log snippet (C:\Windows\Logs\WindowsUpdate.log): 'Rollback started due to installation failure, state: PendingCleanup',
SetupAPI: Found pending file operations: PendingFileRenameOperations contains entries for C:\Windows\System32\drivers\nvlddmkm.sys
Event Viewer System: 2026-03-09 14:13:12 - Service Control Manager: 'Windows Update initiated rollback of pending updates'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SSD replacement plus re-use of same drive signature or prior pending update flag on replacement image is causing Windows to detect an inconsistent component store and trigger a rollback. Another signal: some devices showed driver install failures during the TS (NVIDIA driver) which correlate with PendingFileRenameOperations entries. We reproduced on 1 machine in lab by creating pending file rename entries before reboot and saw the same behavior.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:18 - Priya Nair (Depot Lead): Noted that affected machines were all from the same bin of SSD spares. We tried swapping SSDs and saw inconsistent behavior.

2026-03-11 11:07 - Jonah Park (Assignee): Reproduced failure in imaging-lab-us-west. Confirmed smsts.log exit 3010 then Windows Update rollback. Captured full smsts log and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support-logs/INT-120046/smsts.log

2026-03-11 15:22 - Carlos Mendes (Build Eng): Observed driver install order changed in latest driver-packager job (job #842). Rollback correlates with driver installer returning 1603 on one device. Opened PR to pin older driver variant.
2026-03-12 08:40 - Security Ops: Verified no malware involvement; disk signatures and disk IDs normal. Suggest clearing PendingFileRenameOperations before completing TS.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause appears to be a race between a failing driver install during SCCM TS and a subsequent forced Windows Update operation that tries to clean up in the next boot. The presence of PendingFileRenameOperations and pending component updates prevents the SCCM TS from re-running cleanly, causing devices to remain stuck in a loop.
temporary_workaround: Depot technicians should run the following manual steps after repair before returning machine to imaging queue: (1) from WinPE, run 'dism /image:C:\ /cleanup-image /checkhealth' and clear pending.xml if present; (2) run regedit to clear PendingFileRenameOperations (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager) or run a small PowerShell script to remove entries; (3) reboot to complete cleanup, then re-run TS.
long_term_fix: Update SCCM task sequence to insert a 'clear pending operations' step (custom PowerShell) immediately after driver installs and before Windows Update step. Roll back the driver-packager job #842 to previous stable artifact until updated driver is validated. Add health-check gating that verifies no PendingFileRenameOperations or pending component store state before marking TS successful.
resolution: In progress: temporary workaround documented and deployed to depot techs on 2026-03-12. Driver packager rolled back to v1.17 on 2026-03-12. SCCM TS change (PR referenced above) is under review and scheduled for canary on imaging-lab on 2026-03-15.
follow_up_actions: 1) Deploy TS change to imaging-lab-us-west canary (owner: Build Eng) - target 2026-03-15.
2) Run full sweep of recent SSD-returned devices to validate no residual pending state (owner: Depot Lead) - target 2026-03-13.
3) Add automated health check to provisioning CI that fails pipeline if pending ops detected (owner: Platform Reliability) - target 2026-03-22.
